newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BARESI BACK TO BEST IN MILAN'S 0-0 DRAW AT JUVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BARESI BACK TO BEST IN MILAN'S 0-0 DRAW AT JUVE.

text.p: Veteran Franco Baresi made an inspired return to Milan's defence on Sunday as the Italian champions fought out a scoreless stalemate with Juventus in a rain-soaked clash at Turin's Delle Alpi stadium.

The Milan captain, playing only his second match of the season due to an ankle injury, made crucial last-ditch tackles to deny Juve strikers Christian Vieri and Alen Boksic and help his side keep their first clean sheet of the season.
"There's no substitute for Baresi," Milan manager Oscar Washington Tabarez said after the match. "He gives the team things that no-one else can: leadership and confidence."

In a fiercely-fought but open-ended encounter both sides had their chances. Juve's international goalkeeper Angelo Peruzzi pulled off some superb saves to deny Liberian George Weah and Roberto Baggio, back in the first team after a spell on the sub's bench.

Nevertheless, it was Juve's second-half substitute Michele Padovano who came closest to breaking the deadlock in the 60th minute when his shot from the edge of the six-yard box beat Sebastiano Rossi but not the post.
The result means both sides have passed up the chance to narrow the gap on league leaders Internazionale.
Juventus are level third in the table with Bologna on 16 points, a point adrift of Vicenza and two behind pacesetters Inter, held 2-2 at home to Fiorentina on Saturday.
Milan lie seventh with just 14 points from their nine matches.

Afterwards, Juventus coach Marcello Lippi tried to make light of another display of poor finishing from his frontline strikers Vieri and Boksic, who both shot straight at Rossi in the first half when scoring seemed easier.
"We had our chances to win," Lippi said. "But at least we know we're a highly competitive side so let's see how the rest of the season goes."
At least Lippi's makeshift defence, missing Ciro Ferrara and Paolo Montero through suspension and Gianluca Pessotto with injury, held firm, but only just.
Less than a minute into the match Demetrio Albertini found Weah totally unmarked in the box but, from a tight angle, the Liberian blasted over the bar.
Clearly subscribing to the theory that the best defence lies in attack, Juventus threw themselves forward and, in the eighth minute, Boksic should have scored but shot into Rossi's diving body.
Seconds later, Frenchman Zinedine Zidane volleyed over from the six-yard box with the goal at his mercy.

But for all their pressure and possession, Juventus rarely managed to penetrate Milan's penalty area, where Dutchman Michael Reiziger made a composed debut alongside the irrepressible Baresi, 13 years his senior.
Time and again, Baresi called Milan's offside trap into action or tackled Vieri and Boksic on the point of shooting.
At the other end of the pitch, Weah and Baggio, playing against the club for whom he scored 78 goals in 141 matches, were a constant thorn in the Juventus defence.

In the 43rd minute Weah's sheer athletism created Milan's best chance of the first half but Peruzzi brilliantly parried the point-blank header after the Liberian had thrown himself at Baggio's cross from the bye-line.
At the start of the second half Boksic again squandered a gilt-edged chance, toe-poking over from six metres.
In the 60th minute, Lippi sent on Padovano and the pacy striker instantly made inroads into Milan's defence.
In the space of two minutes he was twice denied a goal -- first by the outstretched foot of Rossi, then by the post.
As Juventus tired, Milan's counter-attacks grew increasingly dangerous and in the dying minutes the visitors twice came close to stealing all the points.
First Baggio, roundly whistled by his old home fans whenever he touched the ball, saw a delicate chip narrowly clear the bar.
Then Peruzzi saved bravely at the feet of Marco Simone, brought on for a tiring Baggio in the final quarter of an hour.
Teams:

Juventus: 1-Angelo Peruzzi; 5-Sergio Porrini, 20-Alessio Tacchinardi, 13-Mark Iuliano, 3-Moreno Torricelli; 7-Angelo Di Livio, 21-Zinedine Zidane (10-Alessandro Del Piero 86th minute), 14-Didier Deschamps, 18-Vladimir Jugovic; 9-Alen Boksic, 15-Christian Vieri (11-Michele Padovano 58th)

AC Milan: 1-Sebastiano Rossi; 14-Michael Reiziger, 11-Alessandro Costacurta, 6-Franco Baresi, 3-Paolo Maldini; 24-Stefano Eranio, 4-Demetrio Albertini, 20-Zvonimir Boban, 22-Edgar Davids (15-Massimo Ambrosini 66th); 9-George Weah, 18-Roberto Baggio (23-Marco Simone 72nd).
